text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended weaker in a correction to the fund-inspired rally earlier in the week. August fell 70 cents to close at $326 per tonne, while October closed $1.30 lower at $316 per tonne. Raw sugar futures in New York closed barely firmer ahead of CFTC's commitments of traders report. The report is expected to reveal an extremely heavy speculative long position, which could bring in trade selling and pressure the market early next week. Traders said speculative rolling of July contracts should add weight to the market ahead of the contract's expiry on June 30. July added 4 points to close at 11.45 cents/lb. October closed 5 points higher at 11.26 cents/lb, while the outer months gained 4 points. Cuban officials said that sugar production in 1996/97 fell below expectations. However, the government has not yet released a final production figure. Most estimates are between 4.1 to 4.3 million tonnes, raw value, down from 4.5 million tonnes produced in 1995/96.

UNITED STATES - Raw sugar imports under the 1996/97 (October/September) tariff rate quota in the period up to June 1 amounted to 1.151 million tonnes. This represents 55 per cent of the total tariff rate quota of 2.100 million tonnes. The largest suppliers up to June 1 were the Dominican Republic (191,538 tonnes), Brazil (163,129 tonnes) and the Philippines (142,798 tonnes).

UNITED STATES - Sugar imports in March 1997 amounted to 218,906 tonnes, raw value, down from the 235,195 tonnes imported in March 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first half of 1996/97 (October/March) up to 1.343 million tonnes against 913,123 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 2.615 million tonnes compared to 1.557 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October/March 1996/97 were Guatemala with 193,528 tonnes raws against 142,319 tonnes, Brazil with 155,972 tonnes compared to 116,780 tonnes and the Philippines with 142,168 tonnes against nil. Largest suppliers of white sugar in 1996/97 were Canada with 19,100 tonnes against 27,713 tonnes and Mexico with 16,928 tonnes compared to 33 tonnes.

Sugar exports in March 1997 dropped to 9,523 tonnes, down from 11,210 tonnes in March 1996. This brought cumulative exports in October/March 1996/97 up to 85,661 tonnes against 169,322 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 310,341 tonnes compared to 504,854 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Jamaica with 17,420 tonnes whites against 21,729 tonnes, Mexico with 12,806 tonnes against 20,478 tonnes and Haiti with 11,076 tonnes, down from 17,966 tonnes.

FRANCE - Sugar imports in March 1997 amounted to 12,586 tonnes, raw value, down from 36,209 tonnes imported in March 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first half of 1996/97 (October/March) up to 180,990 tonnes against 257,745 tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 476,587 tonnes, compared to 364,140 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Reunion with 40,501 tonnes raws, down from 103,621 tonnes, and Belgium-Luxembourg with 26,692 tonnes whites against 20,762 tonnes.

Sugar exports in March 1997 reached 226,336 tonnes against 238,269 tonnes in March 1996. This brought cumulative exports in 1996/97 up to 1.508 million tonnes against 1.696 million tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 were 2.896 million tonnes against 3.067 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Belgium-Luxembourg with 352,667 tonnes whites against 409,736 tonnes, Iran with 178,739 tonnes against 155,650 tonnes, Algeria with 138,529 tonnes, up from 42,532 tonnes and Saudi Arabia with 77,759 tonnes against 63,423 tonnes.

Iraq has agreed to buy 37,500 tonnes of sugar from Egypt at a price of $14 million, press reports said. It was added the Egyptian government will be contacting the United Nations to clear the shipment under the 'oil-for-food' scheme. Egypt's State Holding Company for Food Industries has agreements with Iraq to export goods worth $46 million, including 50,000 tonnes of sugar.
